name: S-Class Veritus Champion
body:
What Are S-Class Characters?

S-class characters are built using the summoner class, as originally presented, as the basis against which all other classes are balanced. The “S” in this case stands for both veritus champion and, as a more appropriate in-world reference, superior. If you have played—or GM’d for—an original summoner and felt it was fine as is, you should have no problem running with an s-class character.

S-class veritus champions are followers of the Sanguine Bond, who pay their blood debts to unknown entities in exchange for dangerous, viscous power.

Role: S-class veritus champions can use their blood magic to take control of any situation, turning it in their favor. Their macabre gifts are a blessing to those in need of help, and a curse when interacting with civil society.

Note: The s-class veritus champion is an alternate, superior version of the unchained veritus champion class. They retain all of the standard veritus champion progressions and options, but some are gained at different levels. Please note these changes when choosing veritus champion archetypes.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d12.

Starting Wealth: 3d6 × 10 gp (average 105 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The s-class veritus champion’s class skills are Craft (Int), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), and Sense Motive (Wis).

Skill Ranks per Level: 2 + Int modifier.

Class Features
Weapon and Armor Proficiency

S-class veritus champions are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, light and medium armor, and shields (except tower shields).

Blood Debt (Ex)

Every s-class veritus champion must pay a blood debt to gain access to some of his abilities. This can be done by dealing hit point damage to himself or another creature as part of a one-hour ritual. For every 3 hit points of damage dealt during this ritual, the champion rolls 1d12 + his Constitution modifier and dedicates that many points toward his blood debt, to a maximum of 12 points per veritus champion level. Hit point damage dealt in this way cannot be healed with magic, but is restored in full with 8 hours of rest if the creature is still alive.

The saving throw DC of any abilities created by converting points of blood debt is 10 + half the veritus champion’s level + his Constitution modifier.

Detect Blood (Sp)

Veritus champions can detect living creatures and the flow of their blood as they grow weary from extended combat or near brushes with death. This functions as detect magic, except as follows:

1st Round—The champion detects the presence or absence of living creatures.

2nd Round—Number of different living creatures, and how many hit points the creature with the most hit points has remaining.

3rd Round—The current hit points and location of each living creature.

Sheathed in Blood (Su)

As a standard action, an s-class veritus champion can convert 3 points of his blood debt into a +1 enhancement bonus applied to his armor, saving throws (as a resistance bonus), or one or more weapons he wields. He can gain up to three of these benefits as a full-round action. These bonuses last for up to 1 hour per veritus champion level. They stack with other enhancement bonuses—such as those found on an enemy’s recovered magic weapon or granted by the paladin’s divine bond—up to a total of +5.

As an s-class veritus champion gains levels, he can convert more of his blood debt into further enhancements, as indicated on Table: S-Class Veritus Champion under the “Enhancement” section. The total effective bonus shared between enhancements and properties cannot exceed that value.

In addition, these bonuses can be used to add any of the following properties:

Armor: balanced, bitter, cocooning, deathless, fortification (light, medium, or heavy), ghost touch, invulnerability, or stanching

Weapon: bane, called, corrosive, corrosive burst, cruel, dancing, ghost touch, keen, speed, or vorpal

Adding these properties consumes an amount of bonus equal to the property’s base price modifier. These properties can be added to any armor or weapon the champion already has, but duplicates do not stack. If the armor or weapon is not magical, at least a +1 enhancement bonus must be added before any other properties can be added. These bonuses and properties are decided when the blood debt is converted and cannot be changed until the next time the champion uses this ability. These bonuses do not function if the weapon is wielded by anyone other than the champion.

Sanguine Endurance (Ex)

At 2nd level, an s-class veritus champion gains Endurance as a bonus feat. At 7th level, he gains Diehard. At 11th level, he gains Survivor.

Spark of Life (Ex)

At 2nd level, an s-class veritus champion gains a +1 bonus on saving throws made against Constitution damage or drain, energy drain, and death effects. This bonus increases by +1 at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level.

Blood Doll (Su)

At 3rd level, an s-class veritus champion learns how to transform the spilled blood of creatures he strikes with his weapon. When the champion scores a critical hit against a creature, or reduces that creature to 0 or fewer hit points, he can spend an immediate action to create a blood doll that he can later sacrifice as part of his blood ritual. If not sacrificed after 24 hours, it bursts (see blood burst, below).

A blood doll is a diminutive undead with an AC of 14, hit points equal to the veritus champion’s level + his Constitution modifier, and no natural attacks. It otherwise counts as a wizard’s familiar when targeted by attacks or effects. The blood doll is blind, but can follow and interact with the veritus champion that created it as if it could see.

An s-class veritus champion can tell his blood dolls apart and knows from what creatures they were created. A willing creature with 30 feet of the veritus champion can allow him to create a blood doll from it by taking damage equal to half the blood doll’s hit points as a standard action. This damage cannot be healed, naturally or with magic, until the blood doll is sacrificed or bursts.

Blood Burst (Su)

Starting at 4th level, an s-class veritus champion can burst a blood doll as an attack action once per round. The champion chooses one of his blood dolls he can see and destroys it, raining gore on creatures in a 10-ft.-radius burst. Each creature in the area must attempt a Reflex save against the champion’s blood debt DC. A failed save deals bludgeoning damage equal to the blood doll’s current hit points and sickens the target for 1d6 rounds. A successful save deals half damage sickens the target for 1 round. A natural 1 on the save creates a new blood doll with hit points equal to half the total damage dealt.

At 8th level, and every 4 levels thereafter, the veritus champion can burst an additional blood doll as part of a fullattack action, giving up an attack for each. At 20th level, he can burst a total of 5 separate dolls as a full-attack action.

Chain Burst (Su)

At 10th level, when one of the s-class veritus champion’s blood dolls bursts and at least one other blood doll is within the burst’s radius, the champion can choose to also burst one additional doll as an immediate action. Creatures in the area of only one doll’s burst are affected normally. A creature in the area of two or more adds all damage those dolls deal together and saves against that damage only once. At 14th level, he can burst up to two additional dolls as an immediate action, and at 18th level, he can burst up to three.

Status (Sp)

At 3rd level, as long as an s-class veritus champion has at least 3 points dedicated to his blood debt for the day, he can cast status at will as a spell-like ability. At 7th level, he can cast greater status instead.

Blood Magic (Sp)

At 4th level, an s-class veritus champion can create a blood doll from the corpse of a spellcaster that has died within 1 minute. When the champion sacrifices any blood doll created from a spellcaster during his blood debt ritual, the doll grants him 1st-level spells known equal to his Constitution modifier for 24 hours. The champion can choose which spells he gains from those previously known or prepared by the spellcaster, and he uses Constitution as his spellcasting modifier when determining DCs and other aspects of the spells he casts in this way. The champion can also choose from the spellcaster’s 2nd-level spells at 7th, 3rd-level spells at 10th, and 4th-level spells at 13th level.

To cast a spell, an s-class veritus champion converts 12 points of his blood debt per spell level at the beginning of the casting (these points are lost if the spell is interrupted or otherwise dispelled).

Blood Biography (Sp)

At 5th level, as long as an s-class veritus champion has at least 6 points dedicated to his blood debt for the day, he can cast blood biography at will as a spell-like ability.

Waves of Blood (Sp)

At 6th level, an s-class veritus champion can convert 12 points of his blood debt as a standard action to cast waves of blood as a spell-like ability.

Sanguine Step (Sp)

At 9th level, an s-class veritus champion can convert 24 points of his blood debt to transport himself great distances via the blood of living creatures. As a standard action that does not provoke attacks of opportunity, he can seamlessly enter any living creature whose size equals or exceeds his own and pass to another living creature within long range (400 ft. + 40 ft. per level). This otherwise functions as dimension door.

The entry and destination creatures need not be familiar to the champion. An s-class veritus champion cannot use himself as an entry creature. If an intended entry creature is unwilling, the champion must make a successful melee touch attack to enter (a missed touch attack wastes the action, but not the points spent).

When exiting a creature, an s-class veritus champion chooses an adjacent square in which to appear. Entering and exiting a creature is painless unless the champion wishes otherwise (see below). In most cases, though, the destination creature finds being the endpoint of a magical portal surprising and quite unsettling.

If he desires, an s-class veritus champion can attempt to make a bloody exit from the destination creature. He bursts forth explosively from the creature’s body, dealing 1d6 points of damage per 2 veritus champion levels. A successful Fortitude save halves the damage. When he makes a bloody exit, an s-class veritus champion must succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or be stunned for 1 round from the shock of his expulsion.

At 14th level, an s-class veritus champion counts his sanguine step as teleport instead, either designating a creature he has at least studied carefully as his exit point, or picking a general direction and distance, appearing out of a random, living creature instead. At 19th level, he counts it as greater teleport.

Blood Possession (Sp)

At 15th level, as long as an s-class veritus champion has at least 60 points dedicated to his blood debt for the day, He can command one of his blood dolls as a full-round action to enter and control the body of any corporeal creature that has blood (or a similar fluid).

This ability functions as marionette possession, but the blood doll’s body enters the target and the target can be unwilling. A successful Will save negates this effect. This ability can be used once per day at 15th level, twice per day at 18th level, and three times per day at 20th level. The champion can end this possession at any time as a standard action. If the host body is slain while the blood doll is possessing it, the doll is immediately ejected, takes 4d6 points of damage, and is stunned for 1 round.

Death’s Reprieve (Su)

Once per day at 19th level, an s-class veritus champion can bring himself back from death’s door. When the champion dies with at least 1 blood debt remaining, all of his blood dolls burst at once, dealing their damage to every creature in their surrounding area (as blood burst). The veritus champion then returns to life at the start of his next turn with no blood debt remaining and hit points equal to the amount of blood debt he lost. Any blood dolls created as a result of the blood burst also rise at that time.

The Sanguine Bond

The source from which all veritus champions draw power is known as the Sanguine Bond. Some speculate that the bond is actually a deific entity unto itself, and no proof exists to support or refute that claim. While the most common veritus champions use the Sanguine Bond to cast blood magic, others prefer to focus more on its supernatural aspects.

All sanguine bonds presented here replace one or more of the following class features: Blood magic, waves of blood, sanguine step, and blood possession. They are available to all veritus champions. These bonds include blood-bonded, blood-born, blood-crazed, and cold-blooded.

Sanguine Bonds

Blood-Bonded (S-Class Veritus Champion Sanguine Bond)
Blood-Born (S-Class Veritus Champion Sanguine Bond)
Blood-Crazed (S-Class Veritus Champion Sanguine Bond)
Cold-Blooded (S-Class Veritus Champion Sanguine Bond)
